record.tranche_reason: Uses the Toy Models of Superposition setup and its feature-geometry measures, comparing the same toy autoencoders with and without dropout.
record.gate_note: Chart descriptions in the text support qualitative results, but exact sparsity levels, plotted values, and most model details are not stated. The reconstruction-performance comparison is not a row because it measures performance rather than superposition or feature geometry.
record.test_reason: Repeats the Toy Models of Superposition autoencoder setup and its geometry and dimensions-per-feature measures. It reproduces the vanilla results and adds dropout on the bottleneck as a new condition, giving results on whether V1's superposition, transition and geometry hold.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes dropout generally inhibits superposition, except with varying feature importance at low sparsity. Dropout makes the phase transition gradual and alters geometry, at a reconstruction-performance cost. A performance-matched no-dropout model still shows more superposition. The mechanistic explanations are labelled speculative.
record.recipe_differences: The post says it uses the same setup as the Toy Models of Superposition study, with dropout added on the hidden bottleneck layer. It also examines dropout's effects on feature geometry and dimensions per represented feature.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with dropout, sparsity, and whether feature importance is uniform or varies. The post also compares dropout levels p=0.4 and 0.15, but does not give specific geometry outcomes for p=0.15 beyond describing it as intermediate in performance and superposition.
record.problems: Exact sparsity levels, most dropout settings for the larger experiments, and quantitative geometry values are not stated in the supplied text. The author notes ambiguity in the dimensions-per-feature metric for partially represented features. The post also reports that dropout harms reconstruction performance, particularly at p=0.4.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The reconstruction-performance comparisons are excluded because they measure autoencoder performance rather than a claim version's feature representation or superposition.

untested.parts: Only 5→2 and 20→5 autoencoders; exact sparsity levels and dropout rates are largely unstated. No real-model or deeper-network tests.
Feature dimensionality in the 1-D vs multi-dimensional sense is not examined; the dimensions-per-feature metric is a superposition-extent measure.
